about: BRIEF58 golden histories for the SEQUENCE limit rule in its decided form of 2026-11-16: kept chains, one search, CONDITIONS CHECKED WHEN A MIDDLE-STAGE ROW ARRIVES (lr.py variant Ki) and again at the final row. Generated by spec/limitrule/rki_golden.py; every expected value comes from running the references (rows_S.engine = today, rows_Ki.engine = the rule, rows_S.engine without a limit = no limit; cross-checked as described in that script). G01-G37 are the cases of LIMIT-RULE-GOLDEN-20261116.json (ids kept; texts corrected where no longer true); G38-G45 are new. One key unless a row says otherwise.

conventions.rows: Each row: stage (1-based), time, event id, row number within the event and stage (expansion index), value, label (used in matches), and key when not the single default key. Events are listed in ordinal order: the ordinal of an event is its position in the list of events (first appearance); all rows of one event share it. Processing order: ordinal, then stage descending, then key, then row number. Recency among rows of one event and stage: row 0 is the most recent.
conventions.window: overall window W: time(final) - time(first) <= W, inclusive; null = none
conventions.step_limits: stage j -> L: time(row of stage j) - time(row of stage j-1) <= L, inclusive
conventions.conditions: stage j -> list of conjuncts, all must be true. ["eq", i]: own value == value of the stage-i row; ["ne", i]: own != stage i; ["gt", i]: own > stage i; ["eq_sum", a, b]: own == stage a + stage b; ["ne_refs", a, b]: stage a != stage b. A null or multivalued operand makes the conjunct null, which fails (ES|QL WHERE). Today's rule evaluates conditions only in the search of a final row. The rule (this file) also evaluates, in the arrival search of a stage-j middle row, every conjunct of stages 2..j on each chain it tries; and the final search evaluates every conjunct again for the chain it picks. A conjunct is evaluated when the lowest stage it reads is bound.
conventions.matches: expected.* lists matches in emission order; a match lists row labels from stage 1 to the final stage. reference_earlier_form_conditions_at_the_end is the result of the earlier form (rows_K, lr.py Kl), for comparison only.
conventions.counters: rule.not_kept_no_valid_chain: middle-stage rows with no valid chain on arrival (order, window, step limits and conditions). rule.not_kept_after_null_evaluation: of those, rows whose arrival search met a null condition value. rule.dropped_at_limit: rows that stopped being kept because of the limit while inside the window (used rows included, as today). rule.left_list: rows pushed out of a list, kept or not. rule.peak_rows_kept: most rows (listed + remembered) one key held. rule.condition_evaluations_*: conjunct evaluations in arrival searches, final searches and substitution tests. rule.arrival_evaluations_null: arrival evaluations whose value was null (the engine may warn for some). rule.arrival_searches_abandoned / final_searches_abandoned: searches that reached a work limit. today.dropped_at_limit: today's counter.
conventions.conditions_widened: BRIEF61 (G46-G50 use these; G01-G45 do not). Further conjunct forms: ["ge", i]: own >= stage i. ["own_eq_const", c]: own == c. ["own_gt_const", c]: own > c. ["ref_eq_const", i, c]: stage i == c. ["is_null_ref", i]: stage-i value IS NULL (true or false, never null; passes on a null operand; a multivalued value is not null). ["mv_contains_ref", i]: MV_CONTAINS(stage i, own): the stage-i value (a list, or a scalar taken as a one-element list) contains the own value; null when the own value is null or multivalued (a model choice: ES|QL treats a null second argument as an empty set, which is contained), false when the stage-i value is null. ["and", spec, ...] and ["or", spec, ...]: composites with ES|QL three-valued logic (false AND null = false, true OR null = true, otherwise null propagates); the stages a composite reads are the union of its parts', and it is evaluated when the lowest of them is bound. A conjunct of stage j that reads no earlier stage (a bare own_eq_const or own_gt_const) is evaluated when the stage j-1 candidate is bound. As before, a conjunct passes only when its value is true.
conventions.new_fields: BRIEF61. final_step_limit: work limit (visits) of every final search under today, the rule and the earlier form (G47; arrival_step_limit is the arrival searches' limit). expected.rule_without_work_limit: the rule with neither work limit. final_search_visits: visits of the search of the last final row. counters.rule_without_work_limit: the rule's counters without work limits. admission: for each middle-stage row, the rule's admission outcome (kept with a chain / kept without a chain because the arrival search was abandoned / not kept). cross_checks_skipped: references that were not applied to the case and why. wrong_if_holder_expired_by_outgoing_step_limit (G50): the result if B0 were expired when its outgoing step limit elapsed (modelled by removing B0). counters.rule.sibling_disagree_same_value (G48): the reference's counter of equal-value siblings with different chains; it compares only siblings whose arrival search completed.

cases.shows: NOT fixed: two stages with a condition; 9 scripts unpacked (x = 1..9), then the first one runs (x = 1). The start that matters is the oldest of 9 starts; at limit 8 both rules lose it. Two-stage queries are unchanged.

Fewer alerts in total than today (the reviewer's history): C0 needs A0 and any B; C1 needs A1 and B1; C2 needs A2 and B2. The rule keeps A0 (B0 remembers it), C0 matches and uses up every B as a substitute; today lost A0 and raises two alerts; the rule and the rule with no limit raise one, (A0, B2, C0). True alerts are not fewer.
Four stages, limit 2, a b c a b a d (where pinned eviction failed): the third-stage row remembers (a, b) directly; the alert is raised.
Plain sequence at limit 1: a b a c. Today keeps only the newest start, which is after b: no alert. The rule: b remembers the first start; the alert EQL raises is raised.
Two stages, 20 starts, one final row, limit 8: no middle stage, so the rule is today's rule exactly (same match, same 12 drops).

A middle event expands into two rows (x 1, x 2). Each row is admitted on its own; the middle stage has no condition here, so admission reads only the event's ordinal and time and both rows remember the same chain. Newer starts push A out of its list; the final row needs the second row's value and finds A through it.

Limit counts rows: a middle event expands into 3 rows at limit 2; its last row (the oldest by the recency order) is pushed out on arrival and counted as dropped. The final row needs that row's value: today and the rule both miss; the rule with no limit matches.

A start event expands into two rows (x 1, x 2). The middle row remembers ONE chain: the most recent start row, which is the first expanded row. Two newer starts push both start rows out of the list; the second start row is not remembered and is dropped. The final row needs it: the rule misses (so does today); no limit matches. A limit of the rule, not a fault.

The final document expands into two rows (x 2, x 1); two starts and two middles. Each final row is searched on its own, in expansion order: F#0 matches (A2, B2, F#0) and uses up B1 as a substitute, so F#1 (which needs A1) finds no unused middle row.

Document X is a start and a middle row (stages 1 and 2). Its middle row is admitted through the earlier start A, never through its own start row (same ordinal). After the match, cross-stage marking uses up X's start row as well, so the second final row finds no start.

Revision 2 case F6 at limit 1: x is a start (expanded into two rows) and a middle row. Today at limit 1 loses a (pushed out by x's start row) and finds nothing; the rule keeps a through x's middle row and gives the no-limit result: one match.
Document X is a middle and a final row. Its final row is processed first (stage descending) and matches (A, B, X); its middle row then finds no unused start and is not kept.
Start, middle and final at the same timestamp, in that ordinal order: order is by ordinal, so the chain is valid and the middle row is admitted.
Middle row at the same timestamp as the start but with a smaller ordinal: no start precedes it, so it is not kept; the final row finds nothing.
Expiry of a remembered row: A0 left its list (limit 1) and B0 remembers it; at t=12 it is outside the window of 10 and expires. Expiry is not a drop: the counter stays 0. No chain is valid at C.
B1 pushes B0 out of its list (limit 1): B0 is dropped at the limit (counter 1); A0, which only B0 remembered, has already left the window, so it expires and is not counted. C matches (A1, B1, C).

Limit 2. A0 has left the list of starts and is kept only because B0 remembers it. C0 matches (A2, B1, C0); A1 and A0 can each replace A2 in that chain, so both are used up as substitutes, A0 although it is not listed. C1 then has B0 but no unused start before it: nothing. Same as no limit.
C0 matches (A0, B0, C0) through the remembered A0; A0 and B0 are used. B0 stays listed with its used chain; C1 finds nothing. B1 is then admitted through the unused A1 and C2 matches (A1, B1, C2).
A middle row before any start is not kept (counter 1); a later middle row after a start is.

One start, 10 middle rows whose condition on the start passes, one final row that rejects every middle row: each middle row's condition is evaluated on arrival (10 evaluations) and passes, so all 10 are kept and 2 are dropped at the limit; the final row's condition fails on every middle row; no match, as today. (The id keeps its earlier name.)

Keys never interact: the start event gives one row under k1 and one under k2; the middle and the final row exist under k1 only for the first pair and under k2 for the second; each key keeps and searches its own rows. At limit 1, A1 pushes A out of the k1 list: today loses the k1 match; under the rule B remembers A.

Unit of use is the row: B expands into B#0 (x 1) and B#1 (x 2), both remembering the latest start A1. Newer starts push A0 and A1 out of the list; A1 stays (remembered), A0 is dropped. C1 needs A0 and B#0: missed (no limit finds it). C2 needs A1 and B#1: found.
A middle row beyond the step limit of every start is not kept (counter 1).
Four stages, limit 1: c0 holds (a0, b0) directly. b0 and a0 leave their lists but stay kept through c0; d matches (a0, b0, c0, d); today finds nothing.
Four stages, limit 1: c1 pushes c0 out of its list; c0 was the only holder of (a0, b0), so c0, a0 and b0 are all dropped (counter 3) and d matches (a1, b1, c1, d).
After (A0, B0, C0) the only start is used up: 8 later middle rows have no unused start and are not kept (counter 8). A1, B1, C1 then match as today.

For the READER as well as the matcher. Limit 2. After (A3, B2, C1) both listed starts are used; A1 is kept only because B1 remembers it. C2 needs A1. A reader that stops when no LISTED start is unused never delivers C2: "is a match still possible" and "latest unused start" must count remembered starts.

cases.shows: Limit 1. Bgood satisfies the middle-stage condition (own value == start value), Bbad does not. Under this form conditions ARE evaluated on arrival: Bbad has no valid chain, is not kept (counter 1) and cannot push Bgood out, so (A, Bgood, C) matches, as with no limit. Today and the earlier form (conditions only at the final row) keep Bbad, lose Bgood and find nothing. (In the earlier set this case was named "conditions-are-not-evaluated-on-arrival"; the statement is now the opposite.)

Limit 1, A->B step limit 2, window 10, ARRIVAL work limit 1 step. Bbad looks at A2 (too far), gives up before looking at the remembered A1, and is kept without a chain; it pushes Bgood out and the match is lost. With no arrival work limit Bbad is not kept and (A1, Bgood, C) matches. Keeping a row whose arrival search gave up is not result-neutral; it is counted apart and never reported as "no chain".

A1 (x 1), A2 (x 2), B (x 1, condition x == MEMBER(s1, x)), C. On arrival the search tries A2 (fails) and finds A1: B is kept and remembers A1. At C the final search tries A2 first and evaluates B's condition again: it fails, so the answer is A1/B/C. Being kept is not approval of every chain: an implementation that trusts admission and evaluates only the final stage's conditions answers A2/B/C (wrong).

A (x 1); Bnull (x null) and Bmv (x multivalued [1, 2]) with condition x == MEMBER(s1, x); C. A null or multivalued operand makes the condition null, which fails as in a WHERE: on arrival both rows have no valid chain and are not kept (counter 2; both counted as "not kept after a null evaluation"; 2 null evaluations). No match under any rule.

Limit 1. Middle event B expands into B#0 (x 9) and B#1 (x 1); condition x == MEMBER(s1, x), A has x 1. Each row runs its own admission with its own value: B#0 is not kept, B#1 is kept (siblings may disagree). Today and the earlier form keep both rows, B#0 (the more recent) pushes B#1 out, and C finds nothing; this form matches (A, B#1, C) as with no limit.

Owner's rule 7, busy installer: a download (x 5), its run (x 5), ONE later event that expands into eight middle rows (x 9) which fail the condition "run matches the download", then the final event. Limit 8. Today and the earlier form keep the eight rows, which push the real run out; this form does not keep them (counter 8) and the alert is raised. MUST MATCH.

NOT fixed: owner's rule 7, re-download loop. A download (x 5), eight more downloads of other files, then the run of the first download (x 5), then the final event. Limit 8. The first download is pushed out of the list of starts before its run arrives and nothing remembers it, so the run has no valid chain and is not kept. Only a larger first-stage limit fixes this.

NOT fixed: two stages (no middle stage, so the rule is today's). One archive event expands into nine start rows (x 9, 8, ..., 1); the script that later runs has x 1, the last expanded row, which is the least recent and is pushed out on arrival at limit 8. Today and this form miss; no limit matches. (G09 is the same with nine separate events.)

Limit 1, condition x == MEMBER(s1, x), ARRIVAL work limit 1 step. Bbad (x 3) tries A2 (fails its condition), reaches the work limit before trying the remembered A1, and is kept without a chain (counted as an abandoned arrival search, never as "no chain"); it pushes Bgood out, A1 is released and the match is lost. With no arrival work limit Bbad has no valid chain, is not kept, and (A1, Bgood, C) matches.

Check k. Limit 2, condition at the final stage x == MEMBER(s1, x). B0 is admitted through Ax (the newest start) and remembers it. C (x 1) matches (Ay, B0, C): B0 is used, Ax is not. Two newer starts push Ax out of its list; it stays kept only because the used, listed B0 still holds its chain. B1 remembers Aq; C2 (x 2) matches (Ax, B1, C2) as with no limit. If a used listed row released its chain, Ax would be gone and C2 would find nothing.

The rule is not a guarantee against today. 21 events at limit 8 (the review, section 1). Stage 2: own >= s1; stage 3: (own == 0 AND (s2 == 0 OR s2 == 3)) OR (own > 0 AND own == s2 AND own == s1). Six P starts push Au out of the list of starts and nothing remembers it, so Bu (which needs Au) has no valid chain and is not kept; today keeps Bu and evicts B0. At C0 the rule matches A2/B0/C0, and A1 is a valid substitute for A2, so both A1 and A2 are used up; C1 and C2 then find nothing. Today raises two alerts (A1/Q6/C1, A2/B2/C2), the rule one, no limit three: the rule finds fewer true alerts than today under either meaning (same members: 0 vs 2; same final row: 1 vs 2). The disjunction in the final condition is what the generated histories never had.

cases.shows: Six stages at the default limit 8 can reach the work limit (the review, section 2). 86 events, window 1000, every stage from 2 on has own == s1. No row is lost (no drop, no row not kept; 85 rows kept). The only valid chain for F is A1/B1/C1/D1/E1/F and the prescribed search reaches it at its last visit: with the work limit 131,072 for final and arrival searches the final search is abandoned and the rule finds nothing; without a work limit it finds A1/B1/C1/D1/E1/F (expected.rule_without_work_limit, visits in final_search_visits). Today's rule finds nothing either (it drops 45 rows), so no alert is lost against today; what fails is the promise that a search is never abandoned at the default.

cases.shows: Siblings with equal values can get different admission answers when an arrival search can be abandoned (the review, section 9). Limit 1, ARRIVAL work limit 1, stage 2: own == s1. A1 (x 1), Bgood (x 1), A2 (x 2), then one event X expanding into X#0 and X#1, both x 3; a final row C (x 0) added so the effect is visible in the matches. X#0 tries A2 (fails), reaches the work limit before the remembered A1, and is kept without a chain; it pushes Bgood out and A1 (remembered only by Bgood) is released. X#1 then sees only A2, fails, and exhausts the candidates exactly at one visit: it is NOT kept. C finds nothing; without the arrival work limit A1/Bgood/C matches. "admission" lists each middle row's outcome, computed by rerunning the reference on prefixes.

admission.X#0: kept without a chain (arrival search abandoned)

cases.shows: A condition can pass on a null and on a multivalued operand (ES|QL IS NULL and MV_CONTAINS; the review, section 9). Limit 1, stage 2: (s1 IS NULL) OR MV_CONTAINS(s1, own). Key k1: the start An has a null value; Bn (x 5) passes through "the start's value is null" and is kept on arrival; Cn matches An/Bn/Cn. Key k2: the start Am has the list [1, 2]; Bm (x 2) passes through "the start's list contains my value" and is kept; Bx (x 3) fails both parts and is not kept, so it cannot push Bm out; Cm matches Am/Bm/Cm. Today keeps Bx, which pushes Bm out, and finds only the k1 match.

cases.shows: A holder must not be expired because it can no longer itself precede a final row (the review, section 6). Limit 1, window 10, stage 2: own == s1, step limit of stage 3 = 1. A0 (t0 x 1), B0 (t1 x 1), A1 (t3 x 2), B1 (t4 x 1), C (t5 x 0). By t3 B0 can no longer precede any C within its step limit, but it is the only holder of A0 (A1 pushed A0 out of the list). Keeping B0 lets B1 be admitted through A0 (B1 fails against A1) and take over the reference; C matches A0/B1/C. Expiring B0 at its outgoing deadline would lose A0 and the match.
